summary: A live bench of the second-factor and step-up flow (tools/fleetbench/bench_idsan_mfa.py, 65/65) found and fixed two real defects on the identity server. First, POST /api/step-up — the endpoint that takes a password and reports whether it was right, to re-authenticate before the most privileged actions — was the only credential-checking endpoint on the server with no lockout behind it; a bench made twelve wrong guesses in 0.6 seconds, all refused, none throttled. Anyone holding a stolen session cookie could not sign in outright but could grind password candidates against it at wire speed. It now shares the same LoginGuard lockout the sign-in surfaces use, keyed on the session's own account, with the same failed-attempt delay and a login.lockout entry when it engages. Second, five audit actions had been declared since MFA shipped and never written by anything: enrolling a second factor, disabling one, spending a break-glass recovery code, and regenerating the recovery set left no trace at all, and a refused login-time second-factor code was filed as an indistinguishable plain login failure. All five now fire from every surface that can produce them — the SPA and server-rendered login challenges, self-service MFA management, step-up, and the WebAuthn re-prove gate. Separately, the RESET_MFA boot-marker escape hatch used to run before the audit service was even constructed, so clearing the stock superadmin's second factor with nobody signing in left only an application-log line; it is now sequenced after the trail exists and writes an mfa.admin_reset entry naming the marker.
compatibility: Backward-compatible; no migration or configuration change needed. Existing installs get the step-up lockout and the five new audit actions automatically on upgrade, using the same loginSecurity thresholds already configured for sign-in. Nothing about a correct step-up, a correct second-factor code, or normal MFA enrollment/removal behaves differently for a legitimate user — only the audit trail and the failure-path throttling changed. Audit history written before this release will show no mfa.enroll/mfa.disable/mfa.recovery_used/mfa.recovery_regenerate/login.mfa_challenge/mfa.admin_reset entries for events that happened prior to upgrade, because those actions were never recorded until now.
